topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Access Optimization
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a multi-level storage structure (registers, L1/L2/L3 caches, main memory) designed to minimize the CPU-memory performance gap. Each level trades capacity for speed, with faster levels positioned closer to the CPU core. Caching strategies optimize memory access latency by exploiting the principle of locality. Temporal locality keeps frequently used data in faster cache levels, while spatial locality prefetches adjacent data blocks. Effective caching ensures high cache hit rates, significantly reducing the average memory access time experienced by the processor.
